title: Layers starting deeper: rock that stands proud goes quiet
question: Is B what you meant by the layers starting deeper -- or were you asking for something stronger, where the standing rock has no visible bedding in it at all?
context_md:
*'Also the layers should only start deeper. Anything above the ground level should be more uniform no layers.'* Same seed, same ground, same palette -- the only change is which cells draw their bedding.

**'Above the ground level' had two readings and I built the one that moves the picture.** Measured against the local column's own surface it changes **209 pixels of 491,520** -- 0.04%, nothing, because the top of a mesa is that column's surface. Measured against the **base level** -- the lowest ground within half a screen either side -- it moves **19.4%** of the frame: anything standing above the surrounding country goes quiet, and the bedding emerges as you look down into the cut.

It fades in over about forty cells rather than switching at a depth, so there is no ruled horizontal line across the faces.

**The materials are untouched**, as you said they could be -- a bed is still its own rock with its own strength, which is what the new relief is built out of. Only the tone is unified.

**Where I am unsure:** whether this is strong enough, or whether the mesas should have no bedding visible at all until you cut into them.
